results.rationale: publish_id is computed as md5(datasource;engine;queryid). Re-publishing the same tuple returned the existing id without a new row. A crafted collision (datasource='x;y',engine='z' vs datasource='x',engine='y;z', same md5) produced a new entity with an already-used publish_id; Spring Data save() on an assigned id performs merge, and Hibernate issued 'update publish set datasource=?, engine=?, query_id=?, user=?, viewers=? where publish_id=?'. Read-back shows a single row for that id whose datasource/engine/user were overwritten (owner changed from 'alice' to 'mallory'). The key still identifies one row, but duplicates are silently converted into an overwrite of the existing row rather than rejected. results.rationale: Predicate 'session_property.datasource has length 256' concerns table session_property, which is only written by query-engine execution paths (Presto/Hive/Spark). Those engines are external services that are not permitted by the verification policy, so the persistence operation could not be reached through the public API.
limitations: Writes to this table occur only after a Presto/Trino, Hive or Spark engine executes (or fails) a query (PrestoService/HiveService -> QueryService.save/saveError, SessionPropertyService.insert). No engine is available locally and the policy forbids external services and any port other than 18209, so no request could reach this persistence operation.
Read-back showed query and session_property row counts of 0 throughout the run.
